mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 5.5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE remains below 5.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) over two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline YoY for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by more than 1% for three consecutive months signals an acceleration in economic output and capacity utilization, which typically precedes positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days due to improved earnings expectations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during at least 70% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above consensus expectations by more than 50,000 in a single month, combined with a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a labor market overheating that increases inflation risk and prompts preemptive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS beats consensus by >50k AND UNRATE falls in the same month
regime_hint: tight labor market with rising inflation fears
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the real savings rate (RSAFS) below its 5-year average for four consecutive months signals increased household dissaving and higher consumption, which boosts demand and corporate earnings, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.3% in the same month indicates a dual signal of monetary tightening and accelerating inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > +0.3% AND CPIAUCSL > +0.3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity and reduced corporate revenue prospects, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
